transcript: Yesterday I saw King Lear at The Shed starring Kenneth Branagh and I thought it was kind of a mess. Lear is a super well known Shakespeare tragedy about a king who basically shuns his favourite daughter after she doesn't stroke his ego to his standards, then his other two daughters give him the cold shoulder, he goes mad, and almost everyone dies. Now, since this is a Shakespeare play, there are obviously way more characters and subplots, but this is the gist of it. I'm pretty familiar with this play and I recognize that there are many ways to put up a Shakespeare but this one was not for me. The direction and the overall concept felt like nothing more than an aesthetic so I didn't feel like there was a distinctive take on the story. Which is fine, but the performances, although serviceable to the plot, were not nuanced enough to truly serve the text. The characters including Lear did not appear to go through the overarching psychological journeys that the text prescribes. And without that depth, the show dragged and the tragic parts did not feel very tragic. There's no denying that Shakespeare is difficult to do well, but for such a well known play, I was at least expecting a more innovative production. With that, another program for my collection.
